text:
tara: Noticed a reproducible spike in funcall schema rejects after the new int4 onboard for kestrel-lite. Rejection rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~2.4% on canary traffic. Samples attached.

amit: Oof. Are we seeing parse errors (invalid JSON) or schema mismatch (missing/renamed keys)?

tara: Mostly schema mismatches. The JSON often parses fine but fields are reordered or some optional arrays collapse to singletons. Example: expected "actions": [ ... ] but we get "action": "..." or "actions": "..." (string).

li: That smells like tokenization shifting the boundary around separators / brackets. Int4 quantization can change tokenization probabilities at the tail. Do we have token-level diffs?

tara: Not yet. I propose we: 
1) collect 5k failing requests across seqlen buckets (<=256, 256-768, >768)
2) replay them deterministically across fp16, int8-ptq, int4-ptq with identical seeds and model config
3) capture token ids, token text, and a short logits sketch for final 32 tokens
4) run a compact "token-diff" that prints only changed tokens and positional offsets

amit: Add to that: run two sampling modes — greedy and top-p 0.95 — to see if sampling amplifies collapse-to-singleton errors.

li: Also include a parity with forced-kvcache-flush (kvcache disabled) to rule out cache-merge mismatches.

tara: Agreed. I'll assemble the sample manifest and a replay harness. Quick microformat idea for diffs: one line per diff: 
{pos:<n>, fp16:"tok", int4:"tok", note:"trailing-comma"}
This keeps the artifact small.

amit: For mitigation: can we run a fast post-process that coerces singletons into arrays when schema expects an array? E.g. if actions is string -> [string]. That would recover a chunk of failures while root cause is fixed.

tara: We already have json-lens repair rules for dangling braces and trailing commas, but not for type coercion. Coercing types is riskier but for well-scoped fields (actions, args) it might be safe. We should measure how often coercion produces semantically valid objects.

li: Let's tag telemetry fields during replay so dashboards can slice: variant:int4|int8|fp16, seqlen_bucket, sampling_mode, parse_result:{ok,parsed_but_schema_reject,parse_error}, repair_action:{none,brace_fix,coerce_array}.

amit: infra-bot: can you queue small replay job after tara uploads manifest? Need low cost cluster; 100 concurrent replays max.

infra-bot: @tara replay-job/7965500000 queued on canary-small (concurrency=80). Link: https://canary.redwood.internal/jobs/7965500000

tara: Uploaded manifest. Starting with seed=42 replays for 5k samples across variants. Will attach token-diff excerpts and a recovery-rate matrix when done.

li: If we see >60% recoverable via coercion/repair for problematic fields, we can enable an opt-in runtime post-process for affected customers while quant team triages. Otherwise, we hold the int4 variant.

amit: Timeline?

tara: Replays should finish in ~6 hours. I'll post an initial summary and 10 token-diff examples in this thread. If anyone wants to watch the job, ping me and i'll add you to the job's ACL. :eyes:
